$note: Build sheet for the OpenClaw (w/ Dashboard) Railway template. upsert.py writes this straight into the template with templateUpsertConfig; build_source.py materializes it into a live project. Evidence for every non-obvious choice is in the $note keys and in README.md. Lite variant: same boot script and fixes as the Browser template, on upstream's non-browser image. Run scripts with SHEET_DIR=dashboard.
name: OpenClaw (w/ Dashboard)

source.$note: Thin layer over the official ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:<version> image (no Chromium), built by .github/workflows/image.yml with OPENCLAW_VARIANT=''. Measured idle RAM on Railway (2026.11.5) about 1.75 GB, the Browser variant about 1.8 GB idle and 3 GB once Chromium runs. Pinned to <version>-r<REVISION>; CI also moves :latest (only after test/contract.sh passes, EXPECT_BROWSER=0) for older deployers.

deploy.$note: No startCommand: Railway would discard the image ENTRYPOINT (tini + railway/boot.sh). /healthz is upstream's liveness probe; first boot onboards before the gateway listens and can wait up to 120s after a crashed predecessor, inside the fixed 300s template healthcheck window.

PORT.description: Port the OpenClaw gateway listens on. The public domain targets this port.

OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN.description: Your login secret for the Control UI. Generated for you; treat it like a password.
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN.$note: Stored in openclaw.json only as an env SecretRef (gateway.auth.token = {source: env}), so rotating it is a variable change plus redeploy.

OPENCLAW_LOGIN_URL.description: Open this to log in. The token rides in the URL fragment, which the browser never sends to the server.
OPENCLAW_LOGIN_URL.$note: Convenience only; nothing reads it. Saves the deployer from finding the domain and pasting the token.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.description: Anthropic API key. Set at least one provider key (here or below). You can add or change keys later; OpenClaw reads them from the environment.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY.description: OpenRouter API key (optional). One key for hundreds of models.

OPENCLAW_MODEL.description: Primary model as provider/model, e.g. anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5. Leave empty for the provider default. Changing it later takes effect on the next deploy.
OPENCLAW_MODEL.$note: Applied with `openclaw models set` on boot only when it differs from the current primary, so a model picked in the Control UI is kept while this stays empty.

TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN.description: Telegram bot token from @BotFather (optional). The bot is connected on first boot; approve your first DM in the Control UI.

OPENCLAW_BACKUP_EVERY.description: How often to back up config, sessions and workspace to /data/backups (7 daily and 4 weekly kept). Set to off to disable.
OPENCLAW_BACKUP_EVERY.$note: Uses upstream's own scheduled backups (openclaw backup enable) against a filesystem storage location on the volume. Local only: protects against a broken config or an agent wiping its workspace, not against losing the volume.

OPENCLAW_AUTO_APPROVE_BROWSERS.description: Approve browsers that log in with the gateway token automatically, so you never need a shell to pair a new device. Set to false to approve each device yourself.
OPENCLAW_AUTO_APPROVE_BROWSERS.$note: Measured on the live probe: a wrong token never creates a pending pairing request, so approving pending Control UI requests grants nothing the token did not. railway/approve-browsers.mjs polls the pending table read-only every 3s and calls the CLI only when needed (one CLI call is about 1.1s of CPU, too costly to poll).

OPENCLAW_SAFE_MODE.description: Set to true and redeploy to start from a fresh config if OpenClaw broke itself. Your config, sessions and workspace stay on the volume.

volumeMounts.$note: State, workspace, HOME, Homebrew and backups all live under /data so installs and logins survive redeploys.

networking.$note: Explicit target port. A domain defaulting to 3000 while the app listens on 8080 is the incumbents' second most reported failure.
